A MANIFESTOWHAT FIELD STUDY TAUGHT ME

A manifesto

I used to think good teaching meant explaining a lesson clearly. Field Study taught me it begins earlier — with a classroom where a learner feels safe enough to ask, to try, and to be wrong.

The Field Study episodes are a series of guided experiences that connect what I learn in my education courses with what actually happens in a classroom. Across sixteen episodes I observed a real school, a Grade 9 science class and its learners — then analyzed what I saw and reflected on the teacher I want to become.

  1. 01

    Learners first. Every learner is different, so I must be patient and flexible.

  2. 02

    Science is experienced. Observed, investigated, modeled — not only memorized.

  3. 03

    Encouragement teaches. Small words of praise change how a learner participates.

  4. 04

    Plan with purpose. Outcomes, activities and assessment should point the same way.

  5. 05

    Keep growing. A teacher is a learner too.

Sixteen episodes.
One evolving perspective.

Each episode opens with a short reflection. When you're ready, open the full episode to see the observations, analyses and learning artifacts behind it.
